b1-alaptorveny-01.title: Communicative Challenge: When Did It Come Into Force?
b1-alaptorveny-01.scenario: At the citizenship interview the examiner asks when the Fundamental Law was adopted and when it came into force.
b1-alaptorveny-01.prompt: Tell the examiner when Parliament adopted the Fundamental Law and when it came into force.
cues: Say when it came into force
b1-alaptorveny-01.target: Az Országgyűlés 2011. április 18-án fogadta el az Alaptörvényt. 2012. január 1-jén lépett hatályba.
b1-alaptorveny-01.english: Parliament adopted the Fundamental Law on 18 April 2011. It came into force on 1 January 2012.
b1-alaptorveny-01.canDo: I can say when the Fundamental Law was adopted and when it came into force.

b1-alaptorveny-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How It Begins
b1-alaptorveny-02.scenario: On a visit to the Parliament building a guide asks you, a visitor preparing for citizenship, how the Fundamental Law begins.
b1-alaptorveny-02.prompt: Tell the guide what the opening text is called and what its first line is.
cues: Say what the opening text is called
b1-alaptorveny-02.target: Az Alaptörvény a Nemzeti hitvallással kezdődik. Az első sora: Isten, áldd meg a magyart!
b1-alaptorveny-02.english: The Fundamental Law begins with the National Avowal. Its first line: God bless the Hungarians!
b1-alaptorveny-02.canDo: I can say what the National Avowal is and how it begins.

b1-alaptorveny-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Dignity and Life
b1-alaptorveny-03.scenario: At the citizenship interview the examiner asks what the Fundamental Law says about human dignity.
b1-alaptorveny-03.prompt: Tell the examiner what the Fundamental Law says about dignity and about life.
cues: Say what the law says about dignity
Say what everyone has the right to
b1-alaptorveny-03.target: Az emberi méltóság sérthetetlen. Mindenkinek joga van az élethez.
b1-alaptorveny-03.english: Human dignity is inviolable. Everyone has the right to life.
b1-alaptorveny-03.canDo: I can name some rights in the Freedom and Responsibility chapter, such as dignity and equality before the law.

b1-alaptorveny-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Power and Duty
b1-alaptorveny-04.scenario: A teacher asks you, a learner preparing for the citizenship interview, how the state is organised.
b1-alaptorveny-04.prompt: Tell the teacher which institution holds the legislative power and name one civic duty.
cues: Say which institution holds the legislative power
b1-alaptorveny-04.target: A törvényhozó hatalom az Országgyűlés. A haza védelme minden magyar állampolgár kötelessége.
b1-alaptorveny-04.english: The legislative power is the National Assembly. Defending the homeland is the duty of every Hungarian citizen.
b1-alaptorveny-04.canDo: I can name the three branches of power and the institutions that exercise them.

b1-alaptorveny-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Guardian of the Law
b1-alaptorveny-05.scenario: At the citizenship interview the examiner asks what the Constitutional Court does.
b1-alaptorveny-05.prompt: Tell the examiner what the Court protects and what it does with an unconstitutional regulation.
cues: Say what it does with an unconstitutional regulation
b1-alaptorveny-05.target: Az Alkotmánybíróság védi az Alaptörvényt. Megsemmisíti az alaptörvény-ellenes jogszabályt.
b1-alaptorveny-05.english: The Constitutional Court protects the Fundamental Law. It annuls the unconstitutional regulation.
b1-alaptorveny-05.canDo: I can say what the Constitutional Court and the Commissioner for Fundamental Rights do.

b1-alaptorveny-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Shape of the Fundamental Law
b1-alaptorveny-consolidation.scenario: At the citizenship interview the examiner asks how the Fundamental Law is built up.
b1-alaptorveny-consolidation.prompt: Tell the examiner which text opens the Fundamental Law and which chapter comes second.
cues: Say which text opens the law
b1-alaptorveny-consolidation.target: Az Alaptörvény a Nemzeti hitvallással kezdődik. A második fejezet a Szabadság és felelősség.
b1-alaptorveny-consolidation.english: The Fundamental Law begins with the National Avowal. The second chapter is Freedom and Responsibility.
b1-alaptorveny-consolidation.canDo: I can say what the Fundamental Law begins with and name its chapters.
